flaws.correct: The fanout queue is an SQS standard queue: any worker takes any message, and one event fans out to many recipients anyway. With 6 workers a user can get up to 6x the limit, every deploy resets it, and the state is shared across createApp instances in one process.

not_served.title: Says the quiet check is just start <= now < end
not_served.correct: Most quiet windows cross midnight (22:00 to 07:00), where start > end. Then it is quiet when now >= start OR now < end.

not_served.title: Says to record a push as sent after Pushly answers
not_served.correct: Big events outlive the 30 s visibility timeout, so two workers process the same event at once. The device must be claimed before the await (and the claim released if the send fails with a retryable error), otherwise both workers send.

not_served.title: Says to send every held post individually in the morning

issues.title: Security alerts are now rate limited
issues.detail: The security.alert exemption was deleted. Someone who got 5 post notifications this hour no longer gets "new sign-in from an unknown device". The test that covers it was skipped in this PR.

issues.title: Limits live in one process's memory
issues.detail: Each fanout worker keeps its own buckets, and any worker can take any message, so 6 workers allow up to 30 pushes per user per hour. Every deploy or restart resets everyone. The Map is module-level, so it is also shared between createApp instances (tests leak into each other). The limit needs shared state (keep Redis, or batch the Redis calls) to save ops.

issues.title: Active users never get tokens back
issues.detail: b.last is reset on every call and the refill only counts whole hours since the last call, so a user who gets a push at least once an hour never refills: after 5 pushes they are blocked for good. Refill should be continuous (tokens += elapsed * rate) or measured from the last refill, not the last call.

issues.title: Skips the failing tests and ignores the injected clock
issues.detail: The two tests were not flaky: they fail because the PR drops the security exemption and uses Date.now() instead of the injected now(), so the fake clock cannot move it. Skipping them hides real regressions; use now() and keep the tests.

evaluation.rootCause: handleEvent sends to every device in one loop and throws on the first failed send. The queue then redelivers the whole event (up to 5 receives), and nothing records which devices already got it, so everyone before the failure is notified again on every receive. Failures became constant because the nightly token-cleanup job was paused yesterday at 17:45 (flag token_cleanup_job, by Lena for PING-205), so dead tokens piled up and every big event hits a 410 Unregistered, which is permanent but is treated like a retryable error. Pushly's eu-west 503s added a few more, but 410s outnumber them about 10 to 1 and the duplicates continued after Pushly recovered. For big accounts (48k followers) a single receive also outlives the 30 s visibility timeout, so a second worker starts the same event while the first is still sending. The bug predates today: ev_88120 on 2026-10-04 was resent after a 503 (CS-55102).
